presets.name: Ink
presets.summary: One near-black glyph on its own pale ground.
presets.description: The plainest the style gets. Worth knowing while you read the rest of these: Glyphs paints its own background as a pale version of the glyph color, so the `backgroundColor` option never reaches the canvas and every preset here moves one color, not two.

presets.name: Sepia
presets.summary: A brown glyph on tanned ground.
presets.description: One color carries both the mark and the ground it sits on, which is what makes this style so cheap to retint.

presets.name: Greyscale
presets.summary: Four greys, no hue at all.
presets.description: Useful for a print stylesheet, a disabled state, or anywhere color would carry meaning it should not.

presets.name: Duotone
presets.summary: One deep teal for every avatar.
presets.description: A single glyph color means every avatar in a set shares both mark and ground, and only the shape changes.

presets.name: Muted
presets.description: The style ships seven saturated colors. This trades them for dusty tones, which suits a dense list where seven bright marks would compete.

presets.name: Electric
presets.description: The other direction on the same lever: colors past anything the style ships. The pale ground goes with them, so the whole tile gets louder rather than just the mark.

presets.name: Cool
presets.description: Half the color wheel. Useful next to Warm when two groups of avatars need to be told apart at a glance.

presets.name: Warm
presets.description: The other half of the same wheel, and the counterpart to Cool.
